Understand DNS TTL and propagation during a website migration
Domains & DNS
DNS changes are cached for a period, so users can reach different destinations while resolvers refresh their answers.
Record the current zone and identify the authoritative DNS provider before making a change.
Set a lower TTL ahead of a planned move where the provider allows it, then update only the records required for the new host.
Keep the old service available during the transition and monitor authoritative answers and user-facing availability.
Lowering TTL immediately before a change does not clear values already cached under the previous TTL.
Query the authoritative nameserver and multiple public resolvers, then check site availability from more than one network before retiring the old host.

The right hosting plan depends on how much server control, maintenance and resource isolation a site needs.
Choose shared hosting for a site that fits the provider's account limits and benefits from a managed control panel.
Choose managed WordPress when WordPress-specific updates, caching or tools are part of the included service and worth the plan cost.
Choose a VPS when you need operating-system control or custom services and have a plan for patching, monitoring and recovery.
